newsitem.title: UK: UK's Diana slips up again with Riviera holiday.
newsitem.headline: UK's Diana slips up again with Riviera holiday.

text.p: Britain's gaffe-prone Princess Diana was in trouble again on Monday for sharing a luxury holiday on the French Riviera with the controversial owner of Harrods luxury store.

Photographs of Diana with her arm around Mohammed Al Fayed aboard his yacht were emblazoned across several newspapers, provoking fury from opposition Conservative MPs who blame the Harrods boss for their fall from power in the May election.

Al Fayed was at the centre of the sleaze scandal that crushed the previous Conservative government after he revealed to newspapers that he had paid several MPs thousands of pounds to ask questions in parliament on his behalf.

Diana and her two sons William, 15, and Harry, 12, are staying at a villa next door to Al Fayed's in St Tropez and she was photographed over the weekend frolicking aboard his yacht wearing a swimming costume and sarong skirt.
She is reported to have known Al Fayed for several years -- Harrods is one of the fashion-conscious princess's favourite shops and her stepmother is a director of the store's duty-free business.
But right-wing editorial writers called her naive for accepting the hospitality of a man who has admitted using his vast wealth to buy influence.
"Mr Fayed is not the sort of person in whose debt a public figure such as the princess should knowingly place herself and her sons," said the Daily Telegraph.
Prince William is heir to the throne after his father Prince Charles, Diana's ex-husband, and Prince Harry is next in line.

"Has she simply failed to realise it might cause difficulty, or is it intended to cause difficulty," asked Conservative MP David Wiltshire. "I think she might be advised to choose her friends more selectively," said another, Laurence Robertson.
Egyptian-born Al Fayed appears to have a warm relationship with the royal family. Last month, he was photographed sitting next to Queen Elizabeth at the Windsor Horse Show, which he sponsored.
Other minor royals are reported to have taken skiing holidays at his chalet in Switzerland.
The Harrods owner has lived in Britain for 30 years but successive Conservative governments have spurned his repeated requests for citizenship.

For Diana the holiday is the latest in a line of publicity gaffes. Last month, she pulled out of a visit to parliament to hear a discussion about landmines after Conservative MPs objected that, as a royal, she had no right to get involved in politics.
A few days later, she had to apologise after taking her under-age son to see a film sympathetic to the outlawed Irish Republican Army (IRA.)
The bad press comes as the woman Diana blamed for the break-up of her marriage is enjoying a spate of sympathetic coverage after being derided for many years.

Camilla Parker Bowles, Prince Charles' lover whom Diana nicknamed "the Rottweiler", is 50 this week and newspapers and television have been applauding the discretion with which she behaved during her long-running affair with Charles.

However, The Mirror couldn't resist pointing up the difference between the tanned and fit Diana in her stylish swim suit and Camilla who was also photographed last week, much less flatteringly, wearing a swimming costume.
